name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,832

entries.clue: Hospital department quick to bandage injury (8)

indicatorNotes.to bandage: a bandage is wound right round the thing it covers, so the word here closes over the letters beside it

blocks.note: pacy means quick, as in a pacy thriller; it opens up to take the insertion
harm is injury done to someone

annotation.surface: A hospital department that is swift to dress a wound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like praise for the department's service and is really the four letters doing the wrapping. Pacy is ordinary British usage for anything that moves at speed.
annotation.definitionFit: The pharmacy is the hospital's dispensary, the department that makes up and hands out the drugs.

entries.clue: Malty hop puzzled expert crossing fields (8)

indicatorNotes.puzzled: someone puzzled cannot make sense of what is in front of them, and neither can you until the letters are re-set

blocks.note: the eight letters of MALTY HOP rearranged

annotation.surface: A malty hop that has even a wide-ranging expert stumped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' begs to be read as an instruction to push one word through another, and it is part of the definition instead. The definition runs to three words, all of them describing the one person.
annotation.definitionFit: A polymath's learning spans several fields at once, which is what an expert crossing fields does.

entries.clue: Creativity without which our world would be what? (3)

indicatorNotes.without which: 'without' takes something away, and 'which' aims the removal at the piece the clue has not yet named

blocks.note: the world we all live on is the Earth
'eh?' is what you say when a remark has gone straight past you

annotation.surface: Wondering aloud what our world would come to with no creativity in it.
annotation.walkthrough: Take three letters out of EARTH and the planet is left going 'eh?'. The question mark is doing real work here: 'what?' is not a vague gesture but the two letters that survive the removal.
annotation.definitionFit: Art is the general noun for creative work, so 'Creativity' stands in for it directly.

entries.clue: Spooner's rude manner, a somewhat dotty way to communicate (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Spooner's: the Reverend Spooner is remembered for trading the opening sounds of two words, so what he utters here has its front sounds swapped

blocks.note: coarse is rude and a mode is a manner; trade the opening sounds of coarse mode

annotation.surface: Someone's crude, offhand way of dealing with people.
annotation.walkthrough: Morse is built from dots and dashes, so 'somewhat dotty' is describing the alphabet rather than calling anybody eccentric. Spooner clues turn on sound, so the spellings either side of the swap need not match.
annotation.definitionFit: Morse code sends letters as dots and dashes down a wire or by lamp, so it is a way of communicating literally made of dots.

entries.clue: City club maybe opening in Islington with volume right up (7)

indicatorNotes.maybe: a club is only one of the four suits, so 'maybe' warns that an example is standing in for the general word
indicatorNotes.opening in: the opening of a word is the letter it starts with

blocks.note: a club is a playing card, one of the four suits
the opening letter of Islington
ff is fortissimo on a score, the marking that tells a player to be very loud

annotation.surface: A London nightclub launching with the music turned up loud.
annotation.walkthrough: Islington is an inner London borough, which keeps the surface firmly in the wrong city while handing over one letter of a Welsh one. Fortissimo's ff is the loudest ordinary dynamic a composer writes.
annotation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital of Wales, so the bare word 'City' names it by category.

entries.clue: Tricky opening golf range (6)

blocks.note: golf is G in the radio alphabet
an ambit is the range or scope a thing covers, as in the ambit of a law

annotation.surface: An awkward first shot down at the golf range.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tricky opening' sounds like the hard first hole of a course, and golf is on hand to encourage that. A gambit is a chess opening that concedes a pawn to win position.
annotation.definitionFit: A gambit gives something away early to gain the advantage, so it is an opening with a trick in it.

entries.clue: Chain with eyelets at both ends (5)

indicatorNotes.at both ends: the letters standing at both ends of a word are the two on its outside

blocks.note: and joins two things the way 'with' does
the outer letters of EYELETS

annotation.surface: A length of chain finished with an eyelet at either end.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface assembles a piece of hardware and 'chain' reads as the metal sort; the answer is a mountain chain. 'Eyelets' is not wanted for its meaning at all, only for its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The Andes run the whole length of South America, and a range of mountains strung out like that is a chain.

entries.clue: Boys initially distribute exam, one marked before new term? (6,5)

indicatorNotes.initially: an initial is the letter a word starts with, so only the front of this word is wanted

blocks.note: the first letter of Boys
to allot is to distribute in shares
the paper is the exam itself, as in sitting three papers

annotation.surface: Boys handing round an exam that somebody marked before term began.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Term' is a school term on the surface and a term of office in the answer, and the marking is a cross in a box rather than a teacher's red pen.
annotation.definitionFit: A ballot paper is the sheet a voter marks with a cross, after which the winner takes up a new term in office.

entries.clue: Tiresome noise from unhappy baby changing sides in cot (6)

indicatorNotes.changing sides: to change sides is to go over to the opposite one, so the letter in place gives way to its opposite number

blocks.note: an unhappy baby is crying
the sides of COT are its outer letters C and T, and it is the leading C of the baby's noise that hands over to the T

annotation.surface: A baby who will not settle, rolling from one side of the cot to the other.
annotation.walkthrough: The cot is not hiding a letter inside it; it supplies two, and only the pair on its outside. 'Tiresome' is the definition, though it reads as more of the same complaint about the baby.
annotation.definitionFit: Something trying wears your patience down by going on and on, which is what tiresome describes.

entries.clue: Force has ceremonial kit covering uniform (6)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover lies over a thing on both sides, so the word goes round what it covers

blocks.note: ceremonial dress is the kit worn on parade
uniform is U in the radio alphabet

annotation.surface: A police force turned out in its parade uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' is the radio alphabet's U, not the outfit the surface has everybody wearing. Duress is force of the coercive kind — a confession signed under duress.
annotation.definitionFit: Duress is pressure brought to bear to make someone act against their will, which is force in the sense of compulsion.

entries.clue: Tesla cracks concrete after flipping further down the road (5)

indicatorNotes.cracks: cracking something open leaves a gap in the middle of it, and the letter drops into the gap
indicatorNotes.after flipping: a thing flipped over ends up the other way round

blocks.note: concrete in the sense of real, turned back to front
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

annotation.surface: An electric car that has flipped and cracked the road surface.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' is the abstract-versus-concrete sense, meaning real, not the stuff the road is made of. The tesla is a unit of magnetism as well as a car, which is where the single letter comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Something further down the road is still to come, the road standing in for time passing.

entries.clue: Trot across circle then pause in circular dance (9)

indicatorNotes.across: to go across a thing is to span it from one side to the other, ending up on both sides of it

blocks.note: to trot is to run at an easy pace
O is the letter drawn as a circle
a delay is a pause in proceedings

annotation.surface: A horse trotting across the ring and then stopping.
annotation.walkthrough: A roundelay is an old song with a refrain that comes round again, and the ring dance performed to it. 'Trot' reads as the horse's gait while supplying a plain word for running.
annotation.definitionFit: A roundelay is danced in a ring, the dancers going round as the refrain comes round.

entries.clue: Attract wrinkly men? It's age (9)

indicatorNotes.wrinkly: a wrinkled thing has lost its smooth line, and letters knocked out of line come back in a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters of MEN ITS AGE rearranged

annotation.surface: Blaming the years for the lines on a group of men.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark belongs to the surface's shrug and the letters run straight through it into 'It's age'. Nine letters is a lot to hold in your head, so count them against the enumeration first.
annotation.definitionFit: A magnet pulls iron towards it, and to magnetise is to exert that pull — the figurative sense is simply to attract.

entries.clue: Powerful car adjusted, muting roars (4,7)

indicatorNotes.adjusted: what has been adjusted no longer sits as it was set, and these letters have been shifted too

blocks.note: the eleven letters of MUTING ROARS rearranged

annotation.surface: An engine tuned so that its roar comes out quieter.
annotation.walkthrough: Gran turismo is Italian for grand touring, the badge on a car built to cross a continent at speed; the GT on a boot lid is the same phrase shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: A gran turismo is a grand tourer, a fast and powerful car made for covering long distances in comfort.

entries.clue: Tin-filling method demonstrated (5)

indicatorNotes.filling: what fills a thing sits inside it rather than beside it

blocks.note: Sn is tin's symbol in the periodic table, taken from the Latin stannum
the how of a thing is the method of doing it

annotation.surface: A tin-filling technique being put through its paces.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes 'Tin-filling' look like one compound adjective, which buries the instruction inside it. Tin's chemical symbol is nothing like its English name because it comes from stannum.
annotation.definitionFit: A method that has been shown has been demonstrated — the same past participle either way.

entries.clue: Criticise dyke builder's mistake after rupture (4,3,1,5)

indicatorNotes.after: what comes after a thing is placed behind it, so the piece named second in the clue is reached first in the answer

blocks.note: a tear is a rupture in cloth
Offa, king of Mercia, threw up Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border in the eighth century
a trip is a stumble, and so a slip or mistake

annotation.surface: A dyke builder blamed for a blunder once the wall gave way.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe moves and Offa's trip becomes off a strip. Offa's Dyke is the earthwork the Mercian king raised along the Welsh border, and long stretches of it are still walkable.
annotation.definitionFit: To tear someone off a strip is to give them a dressing-down, British for a sharp spoken rebuke.

entries.clue: As usual, king enjoying Cambs town's amenities? (9)

blocks.note: R is rex, Latin for king, the letter that follows a monarch's name
anyone making the most of what the place has to offer is OUT IN ELY; Ely is the small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

annotation.surface: A king having a good night out in a small cathedral city.
annotation.walkthrough: Cambs is the everyday shortening of Cambridgeshire on signs and addresses. The long phrase about amenities has to be reread as a place you are standing in before it gives up any letters.
annotation.definitionFit: What is done routinely is done as usual, as a matter of course, and both work as adverbs.

entries.clue: Religious campaigner's vintage blue clothes for Easter (8)

indicatorNotes.clothes for: clothes go round the outside of what they cover, so what is wanted is the letters on the outside

blocks.note: a cru is a named growth or vineyard, the word a French label uses for a wine's pedigree
feeling blue is feeling sad
the outer letters of EASTER

annotation.surface: A gloomy campaigner in the old blue outfit he keeps for Easter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' is the setter's favourite word for a container and is doing something else here — taking the outermost letters rather than putting anything inside. Cru turns up on wine labels as premier cru and grand cru.
annotation.definitionFit: The Crusaders marched on the Holy Land under the cross, so a crusader is a campaigner with religion behind the campaign.

entries.clue: Superficially thuggish crook steals superior Renaissance painting (3,4,6)

indicatorNotes.Superficially: what is superficial is on the surface, so take the letters sitting on the outside of the word
indicatorNotes.crook: something crook is bent out of true, and letters bent out of true come back in another order

blocks.note: the outer letters of THUGGISH, its first and its last
the six letters of STEALS re-set
the upper deck is the superior one

annotation.surface: A thief who only looks like a thug making off with a fine old painting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crook' reads as the thief and is the instruction to bend the letters beside it. The jumbled six run straight on from the two taken off 'thuggish', which is what hides where one word stops.
annotation.definitionFit: Leonardo's mural of Christ's last meal with the apostles, painted in Milan in the 1490s, is one of the Renaissance's best-known paintings.

entries.clue: Like bog Bill is on (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down answer what is on something rests above it, so this piece goes on top

blocks.note: a bill is a poster, and what a poster carries is an ad
a mire is boggy ground

annotation.surface: A poster pasted up over a patch of marsh.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Bill' makes it a man standing in the bog, and it is a printed bill instead. Down clues let 'on' mean directly above, which settles the order.
annotation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to think highly of them, the same warm approval as liking them, and both are verbs.

entries.clue: Harass soldiers repeatedly, time after time (7)

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
OR is Other Ranks, the British army's soldiers below officer rank
the instruction to take soldiers a second time, now as plain men
time again, and this one brings up the rear

annotation.surface: Soldiers being pestered over and over, day after day.
annotation.walkthrough: Two different words for soldiers are wanted rather than the same one twice: the army's Other Ranks first, then simply men. 'Time after time' reads as an adverb and is a T at each end.
annotation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to keep on at them until it hurts, which is harassing them.

entries.clue: Total that is under 100 - someone helping with your golf? (6)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down answer what is under something sits below it, so these letters go beneath

blocks.note: C is a hundred in Roman numerals
to total a column of figures is to add it up
i.e. is short for id est, Latin for that is

annotation.surface: A sum that comes to less than a hundred.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash is where the clue turns: arithmetic before it, a golf course after. 'Under' has to be read as position in the grid rather than as size.
annotation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's clubs round the course and advises on the shot, which is help of a hands-on kind.

entries.clue: Chambers occupied with circulating what lungs take in (5)

indicatorNotes.circulating: what circulates goes round and comes back the other way, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: someone hard at a job is occupied with it
lungs take in air, set down backwards

annotation.surface: Rooms busy with air being moved around them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' sits comfortably in the surface, since rooms are chambers too, and the ones meant are inside the heart. Blood really does circulate through them, which keeps the misdirection medical throughout.
annotation.definitionFit: The atria are the two upper chambers of the heart, where blood arrives before being pumped on.

entries.clue: E in solo transposed up a third throughout (5)

indicatorNotes.transposed up a third: transposing a note up a third lifts it two letter-names higher, counting from the note you start on

blocks.note: doing something solo is doing it alone
count a third up from E — E, F, G — and you land on G, which takes the E's place

annotation.surface: A soloist asked to play the part a third higher than written.
annotation.walkthrough: This is music rather than letters: E is a note, and raising it a third makes it G. The single capital E looks like a stray abbreviation and is the whole of the change.
annotation.definitionFit: Along a road means over the whole length of it, the same end-to-end sense that throughout carries.

entries.clue: Appreciate artist cutting chocolate bar for eating festival (5,4)

indicatorNotes.cutting: to cut into a thing is to open it up and go inside it

blocks.note: a Mars bar is the chocolate bar, opened up to take the insertion
to dig something, in the old slang sense, is to appreciate it
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's standard artist

annotation.surface: An artist cutting up a chocolate bar to enjoy at a food festival.
annotation.walkthrough: Two pieces go into the Mars bar together, which is what disguises where the bar is split. 'Dig' for appreciate is 1960s slang that crosswords have kept in service.
annotation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is Fat Tuesday, the day of feasting that uses up the rich food before Lent's fasting starts.

entries.clue: Detective scrubs face for evening speech (9)

indicatorNotes.face: a word's face is its front, so the letter it begins with is the one wanted

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
to scour a pan is to scrub it clean
the letter at the front of evening

annotation.surface: A detective washing up before an evening engagement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Face' does double duty: on the surface it is the detective's own, in the wordplay it is the front of a word. DI is the rank abbreviation any British police drama uses a dozen times an episode.
annotation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal spoken treatment of a subject, so 'speech' names the same thing as a noun.

entries.clue: Two people checking story admit government stole (5)

indicatorNotes.Two: two of them are called for, so the same piece is taken twice, one on either side
indicatorNotes.admit: to admit someone is to let them in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: the person who checks a story before it runs is the editor, ED
G is the standard abbreviation for government
the second editor of the two

annotation.surface: A pair of sub-editors verifying a story that involves the government.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stole' is the past tense of steal in the sense of moving quietly — he stole out of the room — not of theft, and the newsroom surface works hard to keep you on the theft.
annotation.definitionFit: To edge towards a door is to get there a little at a time without drawing attention, which is how someone steals out.

entries.clue: Quit with rude gesture for boss (3)

blocks.note: to go is to quit a place
the V-sign, two fingers raised with the palm turned inwards, is the British insult, and the letter is the shape it makes

annotation.surface: Walking out of a job with a two-fingered farewell to the manager.
annotation.walkthrough: The V-sign is Britain's own rude gesture, distinct from the single finger, and it is the letter it draws that the clue wants. Gov, short for governor, is how a London cabbie or workman addresses whoever is in charge.
annotation.definitionFit: Gov is the everyday British address for the man in charge, clipped from governor.

entries.clue: Zip shortened on back of costume as much as required (6)

indicatorNotes.shortened: a shortened word has had its end taken off
indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer what sits on something follows it, so this piece comes second
indicatorNotes.back of: the back of a word is the letter it finishes with

blocks.note: the last letter of costume
zip is nothing, a nought, with its final letter dropped

annotation.surface: A zip cut down to fit the back of a costume.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Zip' is the slang for nil rather than the fastener the costume suggests, so it gives nought. The single letter comes first because 'on' in an across clue puts the other piece after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Enough is the amount that answers the need — no less than required, and no more.

entries.clue: Toes vary wildly, accept hosts at bedtime (4,4)

indicatorNotes.wildly: what is done wildly is done with no order kept, so the letters land anywhere

blocks.note: the eight letters of TOES VARY rearranged

annotation.surface: Toes that will not keep still once bedtime comes round.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole of the second half and it describes what a guest does rather than naming it. A comma is all that marks the join between the letters and their meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: To stay over is to spend the night at someone else's house rather than going home, taking up what your hosts offer when bedtime arrives.
